blogs.title: Agentic antimicrobial resistance surveillance with AWS HealthOmics and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
blogs.summary: This post presents a reference architecture that turns public sequencing data into plain-language answers about antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes. It pairs AWS HealthOmics for managed genomics processing with a grounded Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent, so researchers can ask questions without writing bioinformatics code or SQL.

blogs.title: Announcing the AWS Digital Sovereignty Lens for the Well-Architected Framework
blogs.summary: October 2026: This post was reviewed and updated for accuracy. Today we’re launching the AWS Digital Sovereignty Lens, a new Well-Architected lens providing customers with extended guidance for designing, building, and operating sovereign workloads on AWS. Customers tell us that digital sovereignty brings a unique set of challenges that existing architecture guidance doesn’t fully address. […]

blogs.title: Filter, reshape, and redact logs before export with Transformers
blogs.summary: Logpush now supports Transformers, allowing teams to filter, redact, and reshape log streams using SQL before export. Powered by Apache DataFusion and Apache Arrow, Transformers apply those changes directly to log data before it reaches the destination.

blogs.title: Introducing Clef-omni with full multimodality, plus a faster Clef and a cheaper Clef-flash
blogs.summary: We are expanding the Clef decision model family with Clef-omni, natively processing audio, video, images, and text in a single pipeline. We’ve also lowered Clef-flash pricing and boosted Clef inference speeds by up to 2.0x.

blogs.title: Introducing on-demand CPU and memory profiling with flamegraphs for Workers and Durable Objects
blogs.summary: On-demand CPU and memory profiling for Cloudflare Workers and Durable Objects is now available. Now you can generate interactive flamegraphs directly in production to quickly track down memory leaks and performance bottlenecks.

blogs.title: Deno is joining Cloudflare
blogs.summary: The Deno team is joining Cloudflare to radically simplify self-hosting Workers and Durable Objects, so developers can use the same primitives in more places.

blogs.title: Bridging technical depth and usability: The story behind Radar’s redesign
blogs.summary: We redesigned Cloudflare Radar to make real-time global traffic and outage data accessible to a wider audience — including journalists, less technical researchers, and everyday users. By introducing an interactive map and standardized components, we simplified navigation while preserving technical depth.

blogs.title: Building an evidence-grounded agentic security operations harness on Cloudflare
blogs.summary: Cloudflare Managed Defense uses a team of specialized AI agents built on Workers and global network telemetry to analyze security alerts. By separating deterministic evidence collection from model inference, the system delivers grounded recommendations to Managed Defense Analysts.

blogs.title: The keys to the Internet change on October 11. Are you ready?
blogs.summary: On October 11, 2026, the DNS root switches to a new key-signing key (KSK-2024). Learn what this means for you, and how RFC 8509 trust anchor sentinels allow you to test whether your DNS resolver is ready for the rollover.

blogs.title: Spotify More Than Doubled Monthly Code Changes as AI Accelerated Development
blogs.summary: Spotify reports that AI-assisted development more than doubled monthly merged changes, prompting a review of quality and reliability controls across its engineering organization. The company describes changes to testing, observability, rollback capacity, workload prioritization, and automated maintenance as it adapts to higher software change volume. By Leela Kumili

blogs.title: Article: When Should You Use Liquid Clustering? Benchmarking Lakehouse Layout Strategies
blogs.summary: Physical data layout is one of the most consequential decisions in lakehouse engineering. The author compares Liquid Clustering, ZOrdering, and partitioning across four workload types on Delta Lake, uncovering two undocumented failure modes that likely affect production systems today and offering a decision framework for choosing the right layout strategy. By Kushal Kumar Vishwakarma

blogs.title: Podcast: What Does It Really Mean To Program With AI: A Conversation with Joy Ebertz
blogs.summary: In this podcast, Michael Stiefel spoke to Joy Ebertz about how the use of artificial intelligence is changing the way architects and developers do their jobs. Focusing on the long term success of the business is one of the most neglected tasks of an architect. This task becomes particularly important as the nature of artificial intelligence changes the landscape of software development. By Joy Ebe…

blogs.title: Presentation: You Can't Trust Your AI Bill. And Neither Can I
blogs.summary: Erik Peterson discusses why AI spend is eclipsing cloud bills, triggering a major software engineering cost crisis. He explains tokenmaxxing, unit economics, forced developer promotions, and why fully autonomous AI will write, deploy, and govern code by 2028. By Erik Peterson

blogs.title: Java News Roundup: Grails 8, Open Liberty, GlassFish, Infinispan, LangChain4j, Spock
blogs.summary: This week's Java roundup for October 5th, 2026, features news highlighting: OpenJDK JEPs Proposed to Target for JDK 28; Lazy Constants elevated to Candidate status; the GA releases of Apache Grails 8.0 and Open Liberty 20.0.0.10; point releases of TornadoVM, Infinispan, LangChain4j and Spock; and a maintenance release of GlassFish. By Michael Redlich

blogs.title: Context Language Models: Self-Managing Context to Improve Performance and Reduce Compute Costs
blogs.summary: Researchers from Meta, MIT, and the University of Washington introduce Context Language Models (CLMs), a new approach that enables language models to manage and edit their own context rather than relying on predefined mechanisms for summarization, compression, and information retrieval, reporting substantial gains in both performance and computational efficiency. By Sergio De Simone

blogs.title: AWS Introduces Enhanced Custom Event Buses for EventBridge
blogs.summary: AWS recently announced enhanced custom event buses for Amazon EventBridge, allowing organizations to share a centralized bus across accounts with ordered delivery, simplified subscriber management, event replay, content-based deduplication, and a new publisher/subscriber-based pricing model. By Renato Losio

blogs.title: Cloudflare Traces Turns the Proxy Layer into OpenTelemetry Spans, with New Volume-Based Pricing
blogs.summary: Cloudflare has put Traces into open beta, extending automatic tracing from Workers to security rules, transformations, cache, routing and origin handling as OpenTelemetry spans. Traces accept and forward W3C traceparent headers, and Trace Rules allow targeted sampling. Pricing moves to ingestion and retention volume from December 1. By Steef-Jan Wiggers

blogs.title: Android Bench 2 Adds Support for Long-Horizon Tasks, Agentic Evaluation, and Continuous Scoring
blogs.summary: Google has released Android Bench 2.0, a major update to its benchmark framework for evaluating AI models and agents on Android development tasks. The update introduces long-horizon tasks (LHTs), agent-based evaluation, and continuous scoring to better assess performance on complex, multi-step development tasks. By Sergio De Simone

blogs.title: Github Migrates Copilot Runtime to Rust with AI-Assisted Rewrite
blogs.summary: GitHub migrated more than 800,000 lines of Copilot runtime code from TypeScript and Node.js to Rust in about 14.5 weeks using AI-assisted development. The incremental migration used N-API interoperability, automated testing, human review, and 128 pull requests while continuing to ship releases. By Leela Kumili

blogs.title: Presentation: Ontology‐Driven Observability: Building the E2E Knowledge Graph at Netflix Scale
blogs.summary: Prasanna Vijayanathan and Renzo Sanchez-Silva share how Netflix tackles observability across 38M events/sec. They discuss replacing reactive monitoring with an AI-driven operational ontology and agentic workflows using Claude and graph databases. They explain how unifying MELT telemetry into queryable knowledge graphs enables automated triaging, root-cause analysis, and self-healing systems. By Pr…

blogs.title: Cloudflare K2 Builds Event Streams on R2 Object Storage, at a Second of Produce Latency
blogs.summary: Cloudflare has launched K2 in public beta, a serverless event streaming service implementing a durable log on R2 object storage. Cloudflare states produce latency of about one second at p99; a tester reported end-to-end p99 of 7.5 seconds, which a commenter answering for the team said was higher than expected. Consume charges match produce charges per GB. By Steef-Jan Wiggers

blogs.title: Presentation: Multi-Agent Patterns from Spotify’s AI Powered Advertising Platform
blogs.summary: Pratik Rasam discusses how Spotify Ads Manager runs production-grade multi-agent systems at scale using Google ADK Java. He shares key architectural patterns, domain ownership models, deterministic guardrails, and tracing-based evaluation strategies, detailing hard-learned lessons on drawing agent boundaries, optimizing tool schemas, and managing costs while avoiding monolithic agent pitfalls. By …

blogs.title: Technological Sovereignty Requires Choice, Skills, and Support, Panelists Say During OSS EU
blogs.summary: European organisations can enhance their technological sovereignty by developing credible alternatives and acquiring necessary skills, rather than completely avoiding global providers. A panel discussion at the OSS EU highlighted the importance of understanding dependencies in cloud and hardware, and emphasized the need for practical choices in software for effective operational sovereignty. By Ol…

blogs.title: Cloudflare Open Sources Decision Models for AI Agents
blogs.summary: During its recent “Birthday Week”, Cloudflare announced Clef, a set of open-weight AI models designed to choose between predefined options rather than generate text. Cloudflare released 9B- and 27B-parameter models, along with a platform for adapting them to specific decision-making tasks. By Renato Losio

blogs.title: Building Git infrastructure for agent-scale development
blogs.summary: We're rebuilding GitHub's Git infrastructure while GitHub keeps running, creating a foundation for agent-scale software development. The post Building Git infrastructure for agent-scale development appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
